key_insight: Physically informed initialization and loss penalties help origami design optimization avoid basins that perform well continuously but fail after discretization.
engineering_relevance: Biasing initialization toward stiff, flat hinges improves discrete design success without additional compute or changes to the optimization process.
method: Use automatic differentiation in bilevel optimization to select among four hinge types on fixed-geometry origami sheets.
Bias initialization toward the stiff, flat hinge option before optimizing and discretizing.
Alternatively, penalize geometric frustration and mechanical floppiness in the outer loss.
evidence_signal: Relaxed optimization solved 97% of runs, but discrete success was 49% at baseline, 69% with the initialization prior, and 78% with physical penalties.
watch_item: The abstract demonstrates gains on fixed-geometry origami designs; transfer to other discrete mechanical design problems remains unestablished.
paper_title: Physically Interpretable Basin Selection in Discrete-Variable Origami Design
